messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — Dedicated pool dp-us-west-2-1. Tenant `sito-corp` tail latency spike >2s for 6m, error rate 2.8%. Paging oncall. See metrics: https://rwd.internal/metrics/dp-us-west-2-1?sito-corp
Maya S.: oncall here. seeing p95 ~3.9s, p99 6.2s. GPU util at 94-98%.
Chris P.: joining. Is this bespoke batching enabled for Sito? last config shows `max_batch_tokens=1024` and `scheduler=bespoke-slab-v2`.
Lena Q.: confirmed it's a bespoke tenant with dedicated queue. They have high concurrency bursts from a partner integration this morning.
Maya S.: impact: interactive features in Sito's app are timing out for some users. CS pinged saying some pay customers hit errors. Sam R., can you confirm customer impact?
Sam R.: confirmed. Sito support reported ~15% request failures and lots of complaints. They put mitigation on their side but want us to throttle before we roll any risky patches.
Chris P.: immediate plan: isolate Sito traffic to a shaped queue, reduce `max_batch_tokens`, and lower microbatch target to keep latency stable. We can apply a hot config to that tenant without restarting hosts.
Arjun N.: commands ready. Suggested knobs: `max_batch_tokens: 256`, `microbatch_target: 64`, `queue_shaper: {rate_limit_qps: 30, max_inflight: 6}`, and `burst_capacity: 2` for short-lived bursts.
Maya S.: +1. Also enable `prefer_low_latency=true` for this tenant routing so we avoid packing long prompts.
Chris P.: applying changes now to tenant config (hot update). Running:
```
rwdctl tenant update --tenant sito-corp \
  --set max_batch_tokens=256 \
  --set microbatch_target=64 \
  --set queue_shaper.rate_limit_qps=30 \
  --set queue_shaper.max_inflight=6 \
  --set prefer_low_latency=true
```
Maya S.: saw `rwdctl` success output. Rolling to all schedulers that host bespoke queues.
incident-bot: Deploy event recorded: config-hot-update by chris.p @ 2765432275.
Lena Q.: watching metrics. p95 dropped from 3.9s -> 1.6s within 45s, p99 down to ~2.4s. Error rate falling to 0.6%. GPU util dropped to 78%.
Sam R.: pinged Sito support: they report reduced errors, customers seeing improvement. They ask about a longer-term cap to prevent repeat.
Maya S.: short term mitigation looks good. We should schedule a follow-up with Sito to discuss cadence limits and recommend client-side retry/backoff. Also propose a persistent bespoke profile with revised knobs.
Chris P.: filing follow-up ticket: ENG-9812 with proposed permanent config and runbook. Also thinking about adding an automated fallback: when tenant error rate >1% for 3m, automatically reduce `max_batch_tokens` by 2x. Thoughts?
Arjun N.: idea: make that rule opt-in for dedicated tenants. Auto-knob changes are risky but can be gated (canary / revert window). I'll prototype.
Maya S.: agree gate it. For now, mark incident as mitigated. Handing off to next shift for monitoring.
ops-shift-bot: Handoff: Maya S. -> Maya S. (oncoming) at 2765435800. Note: monitor Sito for 2h, escalate if error rate >1% or p99 >3s.
Maya S.: thanks team. final notes in ENG-9812: include timeline, config diff, and customer CS convo link. :thumbsup:
Chris P.: leaving a snippet of the effective config applied:
```
tenant: sito-corp
  max_batch_tokens: 256
  microbatch_target: 64
  queue_shaper:
    rate_limit_qps: 30
    max_inflight: 6
    burst_capacity: 2
  prefer_low_latency: true
```
Lena Q.: will keep an eye on tailers; will run a 30m synthetic load test later to validate before permanent commit.
Sam R.: will patch Sito with recommended client-side backoff and follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT.
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 2765432900.
ops-shift-bot: Reminder: add post-incident summary in #postmortems and update the tenant runbook.
